slides.say: A, B, C and D represent digits. Given: B A, plus D A, is equal to C C A. B plus C plus D is equal to what?
So an addition in letters, and each letter is a digit. [short pause] We'll solve it with our four steps.
[short pause] Step one, write it vertically. Now the columns line up, and we can see things.

Step two, the ones column. A plus A ends in A. Add something to A and land back on A? Nothing carries into the ones column, so that something must be zero. Five plus zero is five, eight plus zero is eight. So A is zero.
at: A plus A ends in A

slides.say: Step three, the leftmost digit. We added two two-digit numbers and got three digits. When you add two numbers and the sum has more digits, the new leading digit is one. So C is one.

Why one? Even the biggest, ninety-nine plus ninety-nine, is one ninety-eight. And ninety plus ninety is one eighty. You can never reach two hundred. But careful, only for two numbers. Three or four numbers can start with two or more.
Now the tens. B plus D gives C C, which is eleven, because A is zero and nothing carries from the ones. So B plus D is eleven. Three and eight, or four and seven, and we don't need to know which.
B plus C plus D is eleven plus one, twelve. Choice number four is our answer.
at: Choice number four is our answer

slides.say: And to see it's real, thirty plus eighty is one ten, and forty plus seventy is one ten too. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
